messages.content: Can you retrieve interface information from the network telemetry API for the fabric named 'test-fab'? I need statistics for the interface type 'gigabitethernet'.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

message.reasoning:
We have to call the tool with appropriate params.

The user wants stats for gigabit interfaces on fabric test-fab. They didn't specify node or pod id; we can omit them. So use url and params accordingly.

We'll produce JSON output as per instructions? Actually they want us to return the result of calling the function. We just provide the function invocation. We'll do:

```json
{"name":"requests_get","arguments":{"url":"/interfaceInfo","params":{"fabricName":"test-fabric","infoType":"statistics","interfaceType":"gigabitethernet"}}}
```

But note the example uses full URL including host. But maybe we only supply relative path? In earlier examples, they used '/interfaceInfo' but also mention base path. Let's follow pattern: Provide "/interfaceInfo". Also param names exactly match those defined: fabricName, nodeId, etc. Use correct case: interfaceType expects one of enumerated values. Provided value 'gigabitethernet'.

Also ensure no trailing slash at end of URL. Good.

Return this JSON object.
